population.canonical: cells whose launch config covers the problem (threads >= n/4) and which move bytes or do flops
population.note_on_excluded_launch_cells: the 9 k_empty cells are the launch MEASUREMENT; they constrain the launch fit rather than being tested against a roofline, so excluding them from per_cell costs the launch term nothing. Reporting them as a separate population is the point: they were silently dropped in the first version of this script, which is the 7% population reduction the review caught.

headline.canonical_population: 81 of 124 anchor cells; the other 43 are the 9 k_empty launch-measurement cells and 34 under-covered cells, both disclosed and both summed
headline.ge_10us_rule: HOLDS as a conservative heuristic, is NOT validated as an analytic predictor, and is not tight. The max-form roofline reaches 17.5% median residual only in the >16M band and 54.5-99.8% below it, so the binding boundary is ~16M rather than 10 us. What makes the rule safe is the SIGN of the error below 16M (over-predicts), not any accuracy claim.
headline.launch_term: helps below 16M (100% -> 28-40% residual) and HURTS above it (17.5% -> 26.7%), because unconditional addition double-counts dispatch on a work-bound cell. The correct form is a regime switch, not addition.
headline.ceiling_sensitivity: the conclusion DEPENDS on the ceiling exactly where the model works: on covered >16M cells the residual is 6.5% at 1538.7 GB/s, 6.6% at the disputed 1541, 19.6% at the 1790 spec and 29.7% at 1200. This RAISES the priority of 6.6.2's ceiling fix.

does_the_ge_10us_rule_hold.why: The >=10 us rule is CONSERVATIVE but not validated: on the canonical population the max-form roofline never reaches 10% in ANY band (best band >16M at 17.5%), so no analytic accuracy claim backs the threshold. What backs it is the SIGN: below 16M the model OVER-predicts time, so treating 'roofline says >10 us' as 'this will be slow' errs on the safe side. Above 16M the model is accurate to within that band and the rule is not the binding constraint.

verdict.design_correction: the bead's DESIGN specifies t_roofline = min(flops/peak, bytes/ceiling). For a fixed amount of work the kernel is bounded BELOW by both resources, so the time floor is max(...). min() always selects the FLOP branch, which for a memory-bound kernel is orders of magnitude smaller, and yields a prediction ~100% low at EVERY size including the largest. Both forms are computed per cell so the difference is auditable rather than argued.
